questionsToConsider: Who reads the responses, how quickly, and does the opening screen say so honestly?
What is your school's route for urgent concerns, and is it written on the first screen?
Should the check-in be anonymous unless a student asks to talk, as this template is?
Has your safeguarding or pastoral lead approved the questions and the follow-up process?
guide.howToUseResponses: Check requests to talk first, every time, and follow up in the way the student chose. Then look at the grid by year group to spot patterns such as poor sleep before exams or a year where belonging drops. Treat the answers as a starting point for a conversation, not an assessment, and follow your school's safeguarding procedure for anything that raises concern.
customizeSteps: Rewrite the opening screen with your support team's name, when answers are read and how to get urgent help.
Change the year groups and the ways to be contacted to match your school.
Share the link at the same point each term, such as tutor time, so you can compare results over the year.

faqs.q: What questions should a student mental health check-in include?
faqs.a: How the student has been feeling, how they are sleeping and coping with work, whether they feel they belong, what is weighing on them and whether they would like to talk to someone.

faqs.q: Is a wellbeing check-in a mental health assessment?
faqs.a: No. It is a way to start a conversation and spot students who want support. It does not diagnose anything or replace a professional assessment.

faqs.q: Should a student wellbeing survey be anonymous?
faqs.a: Anonymous answers tend to be more honest, so this template only asks for a name when a student asks to talk. Make sure the opening screen explains that.

faqs.q: How often should schools run a wellbeing check-in?
faqs.a: Regularly enough to notice change, such as once or twice a term, and at the same point each time so the results can be compared.

doc.title: Student wellbeing check-in
doc.description: A short, kind check-in that lets students ask for support without having to say it out loud.

blocks.title: Hi. This is a quick check-in on how things are going for you. There are no right answers, and it takes about three minutes.
Before you start
blocks.description: Your answers are read by the student support team, usually within two school days. This isn't monitored all the time, so if you need help right now, speak to a trusted adult or contact your local emergency services. Edit this to name your team and how to reach them.

blocks.title: Which year group are you in?
Overall, how have you been feeling over the past two weeks?
Over the past two weeks, how often has each of these been true for you?

rows.label: I've been able to keep up with schoolwork
I've slept well enough to feel rested
I've had someone I can talk to
I've felt like I belong at school
I've had time for things I enjoy

blocks.title: Is anything weighing on you at the moment?
What has helped you get through a tough day lately?

agentHints.askStyle: Keep it light and optional. Accept a short answer and never push for more on a sensitive topic.

blocks.title: Is there anything school could do that would make things a bit easier?
Would you like to talk to someone from the support team?
What's your name, so the right person can find you?
How would you prefer they reach you?

options.label: Find me quietly during the school day
Send me a message on the school system

endings.title: Thanks for checking in
endings.bodyMd: If you ever want to talk, you can fill this in again or speak to any member of staff you trust.

endings.title: Thank you for telling us 💛
endings.bodyMd: Someone from the support team will reach out the way you asked. If things feel worse before then, talk to a trusted adult straight away.

closeRules.closedMessageMd: This form is no longer accepting responses.
